method: Individual preliminary screening; Hebrew text and contemporary translation inspected at exact primary-text locators; no manuscript collation or assertion of dependence. Records are not authoritative until reconciled with merged queue and prior branches.

verses.finding: Marriage with polytheists and concern about calling to the Fire; compare Deuteronomy 7:3–4 with attention to its specific Israelite/Canaanite context.
Menstruation and sexual abstention until purification; compare Leviticus 18:19 and 20:18, not the whole purity regime.

candidates.shared: Intermarriage restrictions linked to risk of worshipping other gods.
candidates.difference: Deuteronomy addresses Israel and specific peoples in a covenantal setting; Quran 2:221 contrasts believers and polytheists, with different legal scope.

candidates.relationship: substantive legal parallel with distinct purity provisions
candidates.shared: Both prohibit sexual intercourse during menstruation.
candidates.difference: Leviticus 20:18 specifies cutting off; Quran 2:222 describes cessation and purification, without replicating Levitical sanctions or its wider ritual impurity framework.

candidates.shared: Both regulate divorce, intervening marriage, and a potential return to a former spouse.
candidates.difference: Deuteronomy prohibits first-husband remarriage after an intervening marriage; Quran 2:230 conditions renewed permissibility on a genuine intervening marriage and its termination.
